set_aside.subject: existing staff-assignment schema after the uniqueness change
set_aside.text:
Creates the tables when absent; never drops, alters, commits, rolls back or
closes.
set_aside.question: When the tables already have the former whole-pair UNIQUE constraint, which module removes or replaces it so that a revoked assignment can be followed by a new active assignment, and what does this operation return or raise until that has happened?
options: This operation migrates the existing constraint, contradicting “never drops, alters”
A separately owned migration updates the schema before this operation runs
This operation detects the incompatible schema and fails with a specified boundary failure
set_aside.default_guess: Use a separately owned pre-start migration, keep this operation non-altering, and make it fail closed with a specified persistence failure when the required schema revision is absent.

witness.initial: The staff assignment table was created by the previously accepted schema with UNIQUE (`staff_id`, `project_id`) and contains a revoked assignment for one pair.
events: `module:portal_store` calls `create_staff_access_schema` on that existing database after the changed design is deployed.
An administrator later assigns the same staff member to the same project again.
outcomes: Following “never drops, alters” leaves the old constraint in place, so insertion of the required new assignment fails.
Treating the changed output as a postcondition requires replacing the old constraint, after which the new active assignment is inserted and the revoked record remains.
witness.observer: The administrator and the `portal_store` caller observe failure versus successful reassignment.
